evidence.description: Customer just purchased home and would like to refresh the basement

comments.message: @Robert Switzer New job assigned and scheduled

Main Topics Discussed

Scope of Work and Client Intentions

The client, Jason Haag, recently moved from Cleveland and wants to improve the basement in a new home (moved in two weeks ago).
The focus is on sprucing up the basement—primarily through painting, not a full-scale remodel.
Jason is considering cosmetic improvements to make the space more enjoyable, especially for home gym equipment.
Walls and Ceiling Considerations

Walls:
The contractor suggests “skimming” the concrete walls (applying a drywall mud-type filler to smooth out cracks and holes), then painting for a clean, updated look.

Ceiling:
No current drywall on the ceiling—just exposed joists and wiring.
Painting the ceiling is an option, but would be more costly and complicated due to masking/taping requirements and painting around obstructions.
The typical recommendation is dry-walling the ceiling and installing can lights, but the client is not seeking that level of renovation.
Decision to paint the ceiling remains tentative; contractor will consult team (Jeff/Neil) for feasibility and pricing.
Flooring Options

Three primary options discussed:
Laminate Vinyl Plank:
Durable, water-resistant, and relatively easy to install and repair.
Not prone to the issues that come with carpeting in basements (such as water damage).
Epoxy Flooring:
Polishing and prepping the floor, filling cracks, then applying the epoxy finish.
Provides a clean, sealed, easy-to-clean finish; good for gym equipment.
Typically higher cost, but considered worthwhile for durability and appearance.
Contractor explains that epoxy is usually done all at once but will check if it can be done in sections (e.g., one half at a time).
Carpet:
Not recommended for basements due to potential water damage.
Additional Logistics and Client Support

The contractor will provide estimates for all flooring (vinyl plank and epoxy) and painting options, with clear line items to allow the client to “pick and choose” services.
Assistance with moving basement equipment and contents will be included as a separate labor line item if needed. Workers will help move items as part of the process.
Measurements taken:
Basement: 18 feet 4 inches (width) × 38 feet 6 inches (length), with 8-foot walls.

Garage measurements also to be included upon client’s request.
